newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka forms citizen committees to help Tamils.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka forms citizen committees to help Tamils.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government is setting up special citizens' committees in the capital Colombo to minimise inconvenience caused to Tamils during military and police raids for suspected Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.

"Every police area in the city of Colombo will have a citizens' committee. Some of these committees have already been set up," Deputy Defence Minister Anuraddha Ratwatte told parliament late on Thursday.
The minister said such committees would minimise the inconvenience caused to Tamils taken into custody by the security forces for questioning.
Police would check the bona fides of these people with the citizens' committee members and release them within three hours, he said.
Hundreds of Tamils are taken into custody for questioning by police and soldiers during regular cordon and search operations in the capital.
Human rights activists say the Tamils are detained for prolonged periods during which they are often harassed and intimidated.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east in a war which began in 1983. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, but the LTTE put the toll higher.
